title: New Resources
paragraphs: Still, it’s amazing how much we managed to earn in such a short time. With the costs of rescuing the villagers and adding Filolial, our expenses must have been quite high. Of course, I contributed through hunting and the Colosseum, but my share was negligible. Come to think of it, this is the first time I’ve ever made this much money in Zeltoble. It might be a good idea to ask Father for some advice on this.
“As expected of you, Father. How can I succeed in business like you have?”

In my first world, hunting was my main source of income. But since the amount you could earn from that was limited to an individual level, I pursued other avenues as well. The Filolial Race, for example, was a way to combine business with pleasure.
“It’s a pain to explain. Figure it out yourself.”
“Please, just tell me! I might be able to give you and the others some advice the next time I loop.”
“Tsk…”
Father clicked his tongue in annoyance and began to offer his advice.
“Well… ideally, you shouldn’t make enemies.”
“Enemies? Shouldn’t I just kill those guys with my spear?”
“…Raphtalia, can we wrap this up now?”
“It seems like this might help us when we loop again, after all…”
Father and the others look terribly reluctant. I know I’m the reason for that, but I don’t really understand what he means by “don’t make enemies.”
“To put it simply, don’t cause a ruckus.”

Don’t cause a ruckus, is that it? Basically, I make a living by hunting and running rampant through mountains and forests to level up Father and the others. But in this case, it’s more of a business matter, isn’t it? When it comes to “the scene” in business, I suppose that means places like markets. As I was furrowing my brow in confusion, Father continued.

“It’s the act of selling items far below market price. Sure, it sells fast, and it’s not a bad tactic when you need cash right away, but if you do it habitually, that price becomes the norm. When that happens, the people who’ve been selling that item all along are the ones who suffer.”

I see. Now that you put it that way, even I get it. For example, let’s say I come back from a hunt with a large amount of supplies. If I keep selling them at a low price, it’ll cut into the profits of those who deal in the same goods. As a result, I’ll end up on the merchants’ bad side.
“But with my abilities, my only connection to merchants is selling the things I get from hunting, isn’t it?”
“Then you should focus on selling items that aren’t traded very often. You can handle that, right?”
Oh, so that’s what they call “rarity value.” It’s true—it’s easy for me to get rare materials from powerful monsters. If I sell those materials, I won’t make any enemies.

So that’s how the peddling that Father did in the first world and during previous loops worked! Back when Father was peddling, he’d sometimes go sell items like potions to places where they were in short supply—but that wasn’t about taking resources away; it was about filling a shortage and earning money in the process. This way, I can do business without making enemies.
“…Ha! Come to think of it, Father in the first world made money by promoting Filo-tan and Keel as Idols!”

He produced massive quantities of all kinds of merchandise and made a fortune. Of course, I was collecting Filo-tan merchandise myself! I had everything—not just the standard merchandise, but every single seasonal limited-edition item as well! I was even planning to build a Filo-tan Memorial Hall someday!

Anyway, that must have been a rare business venture even in that world. You can’t just raid a market that didn’t exist to begin with. In other words, it meant expanding markets that either didn’t exist before or were very small.

“An idol business, huh? It’s not a bad idea if there’s no competition… but if we—who are hiding in Zeltoble—do something like that, it’s practically like asking Melromarc and the Three Heroes Sect to come find us.”

Ugh… These guys are going to get in our way no matter what. I wanted to see Filo-tan in all her glory, but it seems I’ll have to take care of those guys first. After all, the “Filo-tan Idol Project” is something for after the world has achieved peace. I’ll just have to be patient for now, trusting that the day will come when I can see her again.
“So? Are you satisfied now?”

I’ll take Father’s advice and put it together in my head. I suppose it means: don’t take from existing resources; create new ones. With new resources, we can’t take from those who’ve been earning money up until now. In fact, just like the villagers, we could even provide jobs to those who’ve been left out.

“Well, that approach is only for those who want to climb the ranks. Looking at Zeltoble, there’s also a way to make money by making enemies. But that’s too much trouble—there’s no point in us doing it.”
“Even if there are enemies, I’ll take them down. So how about we earn more money and summon Filolial?”
“Listen… we’ve got plenty of enemies already. With the kingdom and religious groups against us, what good would it do to turn the merchants against us too?”
Hmm, I thought it was a good idea, but it seems like a no-go. Still, I’ve come to realize that when it comes to money, Father is the best.
“By the way, Motoyasu, the Melromarc wave is getting quite close. Based on your memory, do you think we can minimize the damage and weather it using Ren and Itsuki?”
Father asks me while looking at Big Sister.

“Since we haven’t been able to share the methods for strengthening ourselves, I don’t think it’s possible. In fact, in the first world, Ren, Itsuki, and I—including myself—all lost to the guy who emerged from the wave.”
It’s not hard to imagine what would have happened if Father hadn’t rushed to the scene. We would have definitely died. That’s the price we pay for treating it like a game.
“In that case, if Motoyasu’s loop conditions were to continue as is, a loop might very well occur.”
Father clicked his tongue. It’s certainly a hassle to go save Ren and Itsuki. Above all, saving those people from Melromarc would be a real pain for Father right now.
“I was originally planning to participate, though. If that’s the case, what should I do…”

Since I’m already registered as Zeltoble, I can’t join the Melromarc wave as things stand. Well, since we know the location, I can teleport there if I register in advance. But I suppose Father is worried that I won’t be able to get there at the exact right time.
“I’ll go to Melromarc in stealth mode and register myself!”
“…Well, I suppose that makes sense. So, Motoyasu, make sure you register properly when the time gets closer.”
“Leave it to me!”
“As for the rest… I don’t know how things will turn out, but I guess all we can do is wait for the Queen of Melromarc to return and for the matter to be resolved.”
“This time, I can only pray that things turn out just as the Spear Hero said they would.”
“Ah… you’re right. Well, to be honest, I’m sleepy. Let’s get some rest before we get started.”
Hearing Father’s words as he yawned, we decided to get a good night’s rest.

From then on, we thoroughly prepared ourselves for the coming wave. Father taught me everything I knew about enhancing weapons, and we learned techniques for controlling Ki and other skills; furthermore, we practiced Magic, and even my Older Sister took the lead in training sessions to improve the villagers’ skills. Of course, using the vast amount of money that Father had earned in such a short time, we continued to track down and purchase supplies for the villagers.

And those with the means went on trading expeditions with Lord Filolial to expand our trade routes. And so… the time leading up to the Wave passed in the blink of an eye. Ah, of course, the Wave that occurred in Zeltoble has already been resolved.

There are now 15 minutes remaining until the Wave in Melromarc. Father and the others are finalizing preparations and confirming the chain of command. They’re organizing the squads with practiced ease.
I’m the leader. Otherwise, we wouldn’t be able to fly properly during the Wave. And Father is overseeing the chain of command. We’re not hiring any mercenaries from Zeltoble or anything like that.
“The wave that’s about to hit will be a chance for you lot to redeem yourselves. But what’s more important—quelling the wave? Or taking revenge on the monsters that emerge from it?”
Father is addressing the villagers as if giving a speech.

“No. The most important thing is to fight in a way that prevents others from suffering the same misfortune as you. You might think, ‘Do we really need to protect those people from Melromarc who did nothing for us?’ But don’t be mistaken.”

The villagers are listening intently to Father’s words. As expected of Father. It’s no wonder he used to be part of the leadership of a major guild. Even though he’s stuck in a loop, he is, after all, the Shield Hero who saved the world!

“Think of this as a practical training exercise—one that includes actual combat—to see if you can protect yourselves and prevent casualties. Make sure you verify for yourselves that you’re truly capable of defending yourselves!”
“I’ll do my best! Woof woof!”
“If Keel-kun’s going to do his best, Luna will too.”

Morale is definitely high. According to Father’s plan, we won’t be taking the approach of going first to quell the waves just to give the villagers some experience. That said, we won’t be taking it easy either—the plan is for us to quell the waves within about fifteen minutes of the start, then let the villagers handle the remaining monsters so we can protect the people. It’s not just about defeating monsters and enemies and then pulling out immediately; apparently, it’s a strategy to make a strong impression on those around us that we’ve truly made a difference, thereby shaking up the Three Heroes Sect of Melromarc and the Trash.
“Boo…”
“Elena, please don’t say you want to stay behind. This is your homeland, after all.”
“Hmph… I am a Lazy Pig, after all.”
I suppose a pig is just a pig, no matter what. In response to my taunt, the Lazy Pig merely glanced my way briefly before letting out a sigh. Father watched this exchange with furrowed brows.
“Speaking of which, Father, how’s the Lazy Pig doing in his peddling business?”

“Hm? Oh, well, to be honest, it’s infuriating, but his results are actually pretty good. I suppose he really is from a merchant family, even if he’s gone to the dogs. Every now and then, he even manages to buy things that can be resold for a high price.”
Father glares at the Lazy Pig. As expected, he’s quite skilled at currying favor for no reason. And to think we could just cull him if he proved useless…

“The downside is that when he’s paired with someone good at negotiating, he just slacks off and does nothing, so it’s hard to gauge his performance. It’s a hassle that it all depends on who he’s teamed up with.”
Oh, it seems Father is keeping a close eye on his staff’s performance after all.

“I seem to recall reading stories about people who don’t want to stand out, or about slackers who succeed—I suppose that’s how it looks to others. It’s not that they can’t get the job done, but I can’t really trust them.”

Father spat out that career advancement happens only in pragmatic circles—or in fictional stories. The reason is probably that even the Lazy Pigs aren’t seriously committed to the task at hand. And the fact that they actually want it that way is what makes them so infuriating.

But forget about the Lazy Pig—it’s all about Filo-tan. Glancing around, I see Filo-tan in her Filolial form, her robe pulled low over her head, crouching behind my Older Sister and her Older Sister. She must be concentrating hard to battle the waves.
Even stoic little Filo-tan is adorable! She flinches and crouches down even lower, curling up into a ball.
“…I really need to mix up some hair growth potion.”
Father suddenly started muttering something like that. I wonder what’s going on?
“Or if the Queen doesn’t hurry up and return, I’m nearing my limit.”
He must be referring to the people he’s taking care of.
“It’ll be fine! If it looks like it’s going to take a while, let’s clear out a spot deep in the mountains and turn it into a village. We can do it.”
“No, I don’t want to go through all that trouble.”
Oh? Father turned me down. Anyway, the time for the wave to hit is drawing near.
“3… 2… 1… here we go!”

At my cue, Father and the others gripped their weapons tightly and charged toward the wave. With a sharp crack, we leaped to the spot where the wave was forming. It brings back memories. Come to think of it, it’s been quite a while since I’ve leaped like this for the second wave.
“This place… Motoyasu was right after all.”

Father looked around and muttered to himself. The sky looked familiar—it was the second wave I’d eagerly challenged back when I was still a fool. Well then, it’s been a while since I’ve seen Ren and Itsuki. Just as I thought that and looked in the direction where Ren and Itsuki should be...
“Well, well! The missing Shield Hero and Spear Hero have finally made an appearance!”
“‘Boo-boo!’”
“Yes… that’s right. It seems the fake Spear Hero is here as well.”
“What!?”

Guys we’d never expect to run into in a place like this are standing right in front of us. There, instead of Ren and Itsuki, for some reason, Takt’s party, the Three Heroes Sect, and the Pope were all waiting for us.
